## x1 profiles of the diffusion coefficients and the mean-of-products face coefficient (`nu_scale_x1`, `kappa_scale_x1`) {#sec-ch09-x1profile}

### Summary

Convection decks often want a dynamic viscosity or conductivity that is constant in height over a strongly
stratified column. In the kinematic form the module multiplies by the face density, so such a deck sets $\nu$ and
an $x_1$ profile $\varsigma(x_1)\propto1/\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}(x_1)$ whose product with $\rho$ is constant. (The
report writes the profile $\varsigma$, because $s$ is the centroid slope of appendix A; see the local-symbol
note.) That balance holds on the faces only if the face coefficient is the mean of the cells' products,
$\tfrac12(\varsigma_{i-1}q_{i-1} + \varsigma_iq_i)$, and not the product of the means: the latter adds a
second-order, always positive excess that makes a conductive or viscous equilibrium generate a tendency, largest at
the top of the column.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Multiplies the kinematic `nu_iso` and/or `kappa_iso` by a positive profile in $x_1$, and takes the
$x_1$ face coefficient as the mean of the two cells' products; @eq-ch09-x1profile-mp.

**Data.** In: finite, increasing $x_1$ knots and scale values; out: scaled face diffusion coefficients.

**Placement.** Built once with the block; read by the diffusion module every stage.

**Activation.** YAML `forcing/diffusion/nu_scale_x1: {x1: [...], scale: [...]}` and `kappa_scale_x1`; Python
`nu_scale_x1` / `kappa_scale_x1` (per cell) or `..._table`. Default: no profile. Refused with `dynamic: true`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Zero tendency for a constant product; second-order face flux; a per-cell profile is refused
when $x_1$ is split; a profile changed after construction is refused.

**Evidence.** Report checks and source-test assertions are listed below; solver ctests were not run at the pin.
:::

**Data details.** In: a table of knots $(x_1, \varsigma)$ from YAML or Python (at least two, finite, strictly
increasing $x_1$, positive values), or one float64 value per $x_1$ cell centre of a block, ghosts included; the cell
field $q$ ($\rho$ or $\rho c_v$). Out: the $x_1$ face coefficients of @sec-ch09-viscosity, and the largest profile
value for the time-step bound. Check cases: a constant product on $n_1$ = 16 to 128, a smooth profile at $n_1$ = 128
and 256, the table on knots and between them.

**Evidence details.** Tests: a constant dynamic coefficient over a stratified column gives no tendency,
{{< code tests/test_diffusion_x1_scale.cpp diffusion_x1_scale.constant_dynamic_coefficient_column_has_no_tendency >}}
($10^{-12}$); the face flux of a smooth profile converges at order above 1.85,
{{< code tests/test_diffusion_x1_scale.cpp diffusion_x1_scale.smooth_profile_flux_converges_at_second_order >}}; the
YAML table equals the per-cell profile bit for bit, {{< code tests/test_diffusion_x1_scale.py main >}}; these ctests
were not run at the pin. Check: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/checks/x1profile_check.py`, output `x1profile_check.out` lines `[C1]`–`[C5]`, re-run at the pin: all PASS, output identical [^env-x1profile].

Local symbols: $\varsigma(x_1)$ [-] the $x_1$ profile of a coefficient (`nu_scale_x1`,
`kappa_scale_x1`; $s$ is the centroid slope of appendix A); $q$ the cell field it multiplies ($\rho$ or $\rho c_v$);
$c=\varsigma q$ the product; $c^{\mathrm{MP}}$, $c^{\mathrm{PM}}$ the mean-of-products and product-of-means face values;
$c_0$ a constant product ($C$[^rg-3f6709e93486] is the Courant number); $F_0$ [W m$^{-2}$] the uniform exact flux of a linear
temperature; $\eta_{i\pm1/2}$ [-] the relative excess of $c^{\mathrm{PM}}$ on a face ($e$[^rg-db37875fae93] is the specific internal energy);
$(x^{\mathrm k}_\ell,\varsigma_\ell)$ the knots of a table. $h$, $\rho_{\mathrm{ref}}$[^rg-bb3732db3865] and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$ are defined in @sec-appa.

A profile is given either as a table of knots in $x_1$, linear between knots and held beyond them, or, from
Python, as one value per $x_1$ cell centre of a block, ghosts included. It is frozen when the block is built.

### Derivation

The derivation is {{< code docs/derivations/diffusion-face-coefficient.md >}} §1, rewritten here in the report's
notation and checked against the code.

On the $x_1$ face $i-\tfrac12$ between cells $i-1$ and $i$ the coefficient is a product $c=\varsigma q$ of the
profile and a cell field, $q=\rho$ for viscosity or $q=\rho c_v$ for conduction. The two candidate face values are

$$
\begin{aligned}
c^{\mathrm{MP}}_{i-1/2} &= \tfrac12(\varsigma_{i-1}q_{i-1} + \varsigma_iq_i), \\
c^{\mathrm{PM}}_{i-1/2} &= \tfrac12(\varsigma_{i-1}+\varsigma_i)\cdot\tfrac12(q_{i-1}+q_i) \\
 &= c^{\mathrm{MP}}_{i-1/2} - \tfrac14(\varsigma_i-\varsigma_{i-1})(q_i-q_{i-1}) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch09-x1profile-mp}

<!-- equation-check: eq-ch09-x1profile-mp ch09_dropin_check.py [D6] -->

The second line is an identity (`[C1]`).[^x1p-c] The code uses $c^{\mathrm{MP}}$ on $x_1$ faces:
`face_scaled_coefficient` multiplies the cell field by the profile and hands the product to `face_coefficient`
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp face_scaled_coefficient >}}), which also extrapolates the product at a wall
(@sec-ch09-wallcoef).

*A constant product.* Let $\varsigma q = c_0$ in every cell. Then $c^{\mathrm{MP}} = c_0$ on every face, while

$$
c^{\mathrm{PM}}_{i-1/2} = c_0\Big[1 + \frac{(q_i-q_{i-1})^2}{4q_{i-1}q_i}\Big] = c_0\big[1 + \tfrac14(h\,\partial_1q/q)^2 + O(h^3)\big].
$$

For a linear temperature, whose exact flux $F_0$ is uniform, the tendency of cell $i$ is
$-(F_0/h)(\eta_{i+1/2}-\eta_{i-1/2})$ with $\eta$ the bracketed excess, $O(h^2)$ in the interior. In the cell next to a wall
one face is the extrapolated product, which is exact, so the tendency there is $O(h)$. The port reproduces both:
$c^{\mathrm{MP}}$ gives $|\dot E|<10^{-12}F_0/h$ at $n_1$ = 16 to 128, and $c^{\mathrm{PM}}$ converges at orders
1.40, 1.66, 1.81 in the interior and 0.71, 0.84, 0.92 over all cells, where the maximum sits in a wall cell
(`[C2]`).

*Round-off of the zero tendency.* For stored $\varsigma_i$, $q_i$, $T_i$ the conductive face flux is
`-kappa * coef * dtdn` with `coef` $=\tfrac12(\varsigma_{i-1}q_{i-1}+\varsigma_iq_i)$ and `dtdn` $=(T_i-T_{i-1})/\Delta x$: six roundings
(two products and one sum in `coef`, a subtraction and a division in `dtdn`, and the two products of the flux),
so each face flux is within $6\cdot\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2$ relative. The divergence adds the subtraction, the division by $V_i$ and the
product with $\Delta t$ of @sec-ch02-laws. To first order the computed tendency of cell $i$ differs from the exact
tendency of the stored values by at most

$$
7\cdot\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2\,\frac{\Delta t}{V_i}\bigl(A\lvert F_{i+1/2}\rvert+A\lvert F_{i-1/2}\rvert\bigr)+3\cdot\tfrac{\epsilon_{\mathrm m}}2\,\lvert\Delta E_i\rvert ,
$$

so the zero tendency of @eq-ch09-x1profile-mp holds to $O(\epsilon_{\mathrm m})$ of $\Delta t\,F_0/h$. The check measures at most 0.056 of the
bound on the 32-cell column of @fig-ch09-x1profile-tendency, where the exact tendency of the stored values, which
is not zero because $\varsigma_iq_i$ is not exactly $c_0$ in binary, is $8.7\times10^{-17}$ of $\Delta t\,F_0/h$. That is the scale
the ctest's $10^{-12}$ tolerance sits far above.

*A smooth product.* $c^{\mathrm{MP}}$ is the trapezoidal average of $c$ across the face and differs from
$c(x_{1,i-1/2})$ by $O(h^2)$; $c^{\mathrm{PM}}$ differs from it by $\tfrac14\,\partial_1\varsigma\,\partial_1q\,h^2$. Both give a second-order face flux (`[C3]`: orders 1.98 and 1.98 from $n_1$ = 128 to 256). The
two forms differ only where a balance should be exact.

*$x_2$ and $x_3$ faces.* Both cells of such a face share one $x_1$, so the two cells' $\varsigma$ are equal and the
two forms are equal in exact arithmetic, but not bit for bit (`[C5]`: relative difference $2.1\times10^{-16}$). The
code keeps the product of means there, `face_average` times `scale`[^rg-e15bb05fefae]
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp face_scaled_coefficient >}}).

*The table.* `profile_from_table` evaluates a table of knots $(x^{\mathrm{k}}_\ell, \varsigma_\ell)$ at the cell
centres: linear between knots, the end value beyond the ends, the knot value exactly at a knot
({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp profile_from_table >}}; `[C4]`). Because it is a function of $x_1$, every block
of an $x_1$ split computes the same values for the same cells.

*Exact and truncated.* Exact: zero tendency for a constant product, and decomposition invariance of the table.
Truncated: the face flux at $O(h^2)$.

[^x1p-c]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch09/checks/x1profile_check.py`, output `x1profile_check.out`, lines `[C1]`–`[C5]`;
    a numpy port of `face_scaled_coefficient`, `face_coefficient` and `profile_from_table` at the pin, double
    precision. Its numbers reproduce those of {{< code docs/derivations/diffusion-face-coefficient.md >}} §3.

### Numerical method

@fig-ch09-x1profile-tendency shows the tendency both forms give on the constant-product column.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch09-x1profile-tendency
#| fig-cap: "Conductive energy tendency $\\dot E_i$ (nondimensional) on a column with a constant coefficient $\\varsigma q=1$ over $\\rho=(1.25-x_1)^{3/2}$ and a linear temperature, 32 cells, from the port of the module. Vermillion squares: the product of the face means; bluish-green circles: the mean of the cells' products, which the code uses and which is zero in every cell. The product of means heats the column, most strongly near the top, and cools the top wall cell."
#| fig-alt: "Line plot of tendency against x1: one curve flat at zero, the other rising toward the top and dropping sharply in the last cell."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch09.figures.fig_x1profile_tendency import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The profile is stored per $x_1$ cell centre, ghosts included, in float64 on the CPU when the module is built, by
`profile` ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::reset >}}), and copied once to the state's device and
dtype on first use, by `on_state` ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}}). A profile of ones
gives the coefficient without a profile bit for bit, because $q\times1=q$. The time-step bound uses the largest
profile value (@eq-ch09-viscosity-dt). The stencil is that of @sec-ch09-viscosity; only the face coefficient
changes.

### Code

**A minimal input.** A kinematic conduction coefficient whose product with a density falling tenfold is constant:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `x1`[^rg-5032dfb16748].
```yaml
forcing:
  diffusion:
    kappa_iso: 0.25
    kappa_scale_x1: {x1: [0., 5.e3, 1.e4], scale: [1., 3.16, 10.]}   # linear between knots, held beyond
```

From Python the profile can instead be one float64 value per $x_1$ cell centre of the block, ghosts included
(`nu_scale_x1` / `kappa_scale_x1` on the options), or a table (`..._table`).

**What is refused, and why.**

1. *A malformed table*: not a map, an unknown key besides `x1` and `scale`, non-numbers, different lengths
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}), fewer than two knots, non-finite values, knots not strictly increasing, or a scale not
   strictly positive (`checked_table`, {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}).
2. *At setup:* an inference tensor; a profile given both per cell and as a table; any profile with `dynamic: true`,
   which has no density to balance; a per-cell profile when $x_1$ is split, of the wrong length, not float64, or not
   finite and positive (`DiffusionImpl::reset`, {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}).
3. *After setup:* a profile set, replaced or changed after the block was built (`check_profiles`, {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp >}}).

**The code, mapped to @eq-ch09-x1profile-mp** (`face_scaled_coefficient`, $x_1$ faces):

```cpp
if (idir == 0) {
  return face_coefficient(value * scale.view({1, 1, -1}), coord, idir, start,
                          end, wall_lower, wall_upper);
}
```

`value * scale` is the product $\varsigma q$ in every cell, so `face_coefficient` returns $c^{\mathrm{MP}}$ on interior faces (its
`face_average`) and the extrapolated product on a wall face (@sec-ch09-wallcoef).

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| YAML table parsing | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `take_table` | `nu_scale_x1`, `kappa_scale_x1` |
| table checks | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp checked_table >}} | `checked_table` | |
| table at the centres | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp profile_from_table >}} | `profile_from_table` | |
| build, refusals | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::reset >}} | `profile` | per cell or table |
| frozen after build | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::check_profiles >}} | `check_profiles` | |
| @eq-ch09-x1profile-mp on $x_1$ faces | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp face_scaled_coefficient >}} | `face_scaled_coefficient` | |
| $x_2$/$x_3$ faces | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp face_scaled_coefficient >}} | `face_average` | |
| use in the fluxes | {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}} | `face_scaled_coefficient` | profile given |

: Code map of the $x_1$ coefficient profiles. {#tbl-ch09-x1profile-code}

1. `from_yaml` reads a table `{x1, scale}` and checks it with `checked_table`: at least two knots, finite, strictly
   increasing $x_1$, positive values ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}},
   {{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp checked_table >}}).
2. `reset` refuses an inference tensor, a profile given both ways, any profile with `dynamic: true`, and a per-cell
   profile when $x_1$ is split into several blocks, of the wrong length, not float64, or not positive
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::reset >}}).
3. At every `forward` and `max_time_step`, `check_profiles` refuses a profile set, replaced or changed after the
   block was built, by identity, version counter and value
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::check_profiles >}}).
4. `forward` uses `face_scaled_coefficient` in place of `face_coefficient` when a profile is set
   ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::forward >}}).

### Limits

1. **Per-cell profiles on one $x_1$ block only.** A per-cell tensor covers one block's cells, so it is refused when
   $x_1$ is split, `nb1`[^rg-254203656f50] $>1$ ({{< code src/forcing/diffusion.cpp DiffusionImpl::reset >}}); use a table.
2. **Kinematic form only.** A profile is refused with `dynamic: true`, which has no density to balance.
3. **Frozen.** A profile changed after the block is built is refused, not used.
4. **The table is linear between knots**; a profile with curvature needs enough knots. Not measured.
5. **The wall cell keeps the $O(h)$ error** of the normal-stress kernel (@sec-ch09-viscosity).


[^env-x1profile]: Recorded run environment: Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.
